correct_completion: the manager sent it to the board before lunch.
full_sentence: Having finished the report, the manager sent it to the board before lunch.
acceptable_variants: the manager then delivered it to the board before lunch.
the manager called the board to present it before lunch.

options.text: the board finished the report before lunch.
options.why_wrong: The participle clause 'Having finished the report' must refer to the main subject. Here the board would be the one finishing, which makes the sentence illogical.

options.text: the report was sent to the board before lunch.
options.why_wrong: The report cannot be the one that finished itself, so the subject of the participle clause does not match the main clause.

options.text: the manager sent it to the board before lunch.
to send it to the board before lunch.
options.why_wrong: This is an infinitive fragment with no finite verb after the comma, so it cannot complete the sentence as a main clause.

grammar_focus: Participle clauses with a matching subject
explanation: A participle clause at the start of a sentence describes an action completed before the main action. Its implied subject must be the same as the subject of the main clause, which is the manager in this case.
translation: Skończywszy raport, menedżer wysłał go do zarządu przed lunchem.
